lines: GHC Scholarships for Students and Faculty 2020
Follow this page to get timely alerts on

AnitaB.org invites applications for GHC Scholarships for Students and Faculty 2020 from female undergraduate, graduate students and faculty. The scholarship aims to provide funds for eligible female candidates to attend the celebration. Selected students will get variable benefits.
To be eligible, an applicant must:
Be at least 18 years of age by September 29, 2020
Be a full-time student enrolled in an accredited degree program at a college, university, or high school at the time of applying
Be a full-time student enrolled in an accredited degree program at a college or university at the time of the Celebration (September 29 — October 2, 2020) (
: Those graduating prior to the Celebration are not eligible unless accepted to another related degree program such as an M.S. or PhD program)

Show satisfactory progress toward a degree such as, but not limited to, computer science, computer engineering, or a related technical discipline such as electrical engineering, human-computer interaction, math, physics, or management information systems
Be able to demonstrate an interest in computing
Not have been an AnitaB.org-GHC Scholar in 2019
Be teaching at an accredited college or university at the time of the conference

Teach in a degree program such as, but not limited to, computer science, computer engineering, or a related technical discipline such as electrical engineering, human-computer interaction, math, physics, or management information systems
Stipend (to be used for travel, meals, and incidentals such as rideshares, baggage fees, etc.)
Follow the steps below to apply for the scholarship:
Notification of status to applicants: Early May
Selection will be based on the eligibility criteria.
Faculty recommendations are accepted from full-time: Lecturers/Non-tenure track, Associate Professors, Assistant Professors, or Professors.
The organization does not accept recommendations from supervisors, mentors, or teaching assistants.
International scholars must pay for their visas at their own expense.
Women who get selected as scholars gain access to career and academic workshops, networking opportunities, and memories that will last a lifetime.
